title: Jonas Jerebko
wikitext:
'''Jonas Jerebko''' (born March 2, 1987 in [[Borås]], [[Sweden]]) is a [[Sweden|Swedish]] professional [[basketball player]]. He is 6 ft 8.25 in (2.04 m) tall and he weighs 232 pounds (105 kg). He plays at the [[Small forward (basketball)|small forward]] position. He is currently playing with the [[Lega A]] team [[Pallacanestro Biella]].

==Early years==
He is the son of former [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse University]] player Chris Jerebko, who played professionally in Sweden and settled in that country. In 2005, he signed a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] to play [[college basketball|U.S. college basketball]] for the [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|University at Buffalo]] in his father's hometown. However, he decided to give up his [[athletic scholarship|scholarship]] in favor of a professional career.<ref name=Fraschilla>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2009/columns/story?columnist=fraschilla_fran&page=nbadraft-090520 |title=NBA draft: Top 5 European prospects |first=Fran |last=Fraschilla |authorlink=Fran Fraschilla |publisher=''[[ESPN.com]]'' |date=2009-05-20 |accessdate=2009-06-05}}</ref>

==Pro career==
Jerebko began his career playing with the [[Ligan|Swedish League]] club [[Borås Basket]] and in the 2006-07 season he moved to the reigning Swedish champion team [[Plannja Basket]], where he also won a Swedish championship. He then moved to the Italian [[Lega A]] club [[Pallacanestro Biella]] in 2007. He declared that he would enter the [[2008 NBA Draft]], but later withdrew, stating that he wanted to spend one more year in the Italian League to gain more experience before entering the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]. Former college coach and current [[ESPN]] analyst [[Fran Fraschilla]] considers Jerebko one of the top five European prospects in the [[2009 NBA Draft|2009 draft]].<ref name=Fraschilla/>

==Swedish national team==
Jerebko currently has 10 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] with the [[Sweden national basketball team|Swedish national basketball team]].
